title: Chüzan
capsule: Chūzan was one of three rival kingdoms of the Sanzan period on Okinawa, based at Urasoe Castle, that emerged around 1314 as regional lords fractured the island's political structure. King Satto (r. c. 1355–1397) transformed Chūzan into a recognized Ming tributary from 1372, establishing Kumemura as a settlement of Chinese immigrant officials and inaugurating the maritime diplomacy that would define Ryukyuan statecraft. The aji Hashi seized power through his father Shishō c. 1407, conquered Hokuzan in 1419 and Nanzan in 1429, and unified Okinawa as the Ryukyu Kingdom under the Ming-granted dynastic name Shō.
